items.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: The singer was, he was a pretty good singer but he wasn’t powerful like David Clayton Thomas or one of those guys

ctx.x: Were Blood Sweat & Tears and Chicago a reason for some of those things?

I think they were a definite reason for Dreams. I think Dreams was a band that was, I mean the guys liked to play that way, but the band was also put together to try to be successful. I mean they saw the success of Blood, Sweat & Tears and Randy Brecker had been in Blood Sweat & Tears and actually left before the band went gold. I mean he did an album with them called “The Child Is Father To The Man,” and then he quit, he said I don’t want to do this stuff, and then Lew Soloff took the gig and Lew was on the…

the strangest thing in the world. And we recorded them for Ahmad Jamal’s record label, which I think was called AJP Records, which I think had our record on it and maybe one other record and then went bankrupt. My mother is the only person with a copy of this record. It was just hysterical things that I was involved in. And then finally in the early 70s I moved to New York to play with Chico Hamilton on a recommendation from a friend who was leaving the band. And that’s when I moved to stay. And then I never went…
